questions.question: Which of the following do you NOT need to check before riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Make sure the headlight works.
Check the oil level.
Test both brakes to make sure the brake light comes on.
Check if the paint is scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if the paint is scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition. Check your oil and fluid levels. Make sure your headlight, taillight, turn signals, and brake light all work properly.

questions.question: When riding past parked cars, what should you be ready for?

options.text: Empty parking spaces.
A car suddenly pulling out into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers seeing you and staying out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car can suddenly pull out in front of you. Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space to avoid danger.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride more slowly than usual.
Wait longer before slowing down.
Try to fit into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Your bike will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride slower, start braking sooner, keep more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: Riding next to a car:

options.text: Is a good idea.
Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is only unsafe when the road is wet.
Makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly beside another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the car blocks your escape route.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery for motorcycles?

options.text: Wet pavement
A driveway
Dry pavement
A parking lot

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Always ride carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: Who is most likely to have a motorcycle crash?

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often with new riders who don't have training and don't know their motorcycle.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing gloves while riding?

options.text: They make the motorcycle harder to control and should be avoided.
They help other drivers see you.
They improve your grip on the handlebars.
They provide no protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: They improve your grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on your handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols.
Blue with white lettering or symbols.
White with black lettering or symbols.
White with red lettering or symbols.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How can you ride safely at night?

options.text: Avoid riding at night.
Wear reflective clothing.
Only ride in the city.
Ride faster so drivers can see your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night to make yourself more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Ignore them.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate faster and increases danger.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way down to neutral first.
Accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Shift down one gear at a time. Ease out the clutch slowly between each shift.

questions.question: When it is clear you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if there are nearby pedestrians.
Only need to use a turn signal if you are at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Use it even if you think your intention is obvious. Other vehicles nearby may not see you.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants:

options.text: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
Should be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Should only partially cover your arms and legs.
Should be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather provides the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?

options.text: A gravel road
Dry pavement
Mud
Lane markings

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Dry pavement offers the best grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are all hazardous for motorcycles.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
Side effects may still remain.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system. This buildup can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Protect only your eyes.
Work as well as a face shield.
Offer the same protection as a windshield.
Protect your entire face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield protects your whole face and is better. A windshield does not replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Look only at your mirrors.
Rely on your peripheral vision.
Slow down so vehicles in your blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder for vehicles before you change lanes.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Allows you to see far to the sides for safe riding.
Looks good.
Does not have a chin strap.
Protects your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to see far to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A Department of Transportation-approved helmet will not limit your vision. You can see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up.
Ride faster.
Ride on the shoulder.
Pull off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. Take rest breaks every two hours on long trips to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Wool
Polyester

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.
